hypothesis: H3 (Qwen3-VL text side) follows colour names bound to objects at least as well as HEX codes bound to the same objects; HEX gives no closer palette match to the card.
single_variable: Colour token form only (HEX vs colour name); same five objects, same order, same sentence frame.

body_keys_seen_in_repo_scripts: prompt (single string = the assembled prompt below)
freevideo.confirm_note: How FreeVideo distinguishes i2va first frame vs Ref2VA reference (and whether a 'task type' key exists) is NOT verified; inspect /plan response before /jobs. If /plan width/height or frame count differ from expected, stop and report; do not submit.

blind_protocol.submitter: Haiku-S (submits jobs, extracts frames, runs objective scripts). Sees prompts; never rates.
blind_protocol.rater: Haiku-R (different agent instance). Sees only code-named media + rater_brief + rubric, in E:/MinimaxH3/_blind/<test-id>/ (outside the repo). Must not read the repo, plan.json, jobs.json or FreeVideo labels.
blind_protocol.codes: Main session draws a random 6-char [a-z0-9] code per (arm, seed) with secrets.token_hex, writes the key to workspace/experiments/_local/<test-id>/key.json (gitignored), and gives Haiku-S only code -> prompt-file mapping. FreeVideo ref = <test-id>-<code>-<yyyymmddHHMM>; label = test id + code, never arm letters.
blind_protocol.order: Main session shuffles clip order separately for the rater.
blind_protocol.unblinding: Only after scores.csv and metrics.csv are committed to the working tree; then main session copies key.json into summary.md.
known_leaks: HEX arm may render '#0B1118'-style text or colour swatches in frame, which unblinds the rater. Therefore the objective card dE76 is the deciding metric; blind scores are secondary.

A.prompt:
integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, low-saturation dusk realism. A medium-wide shot at eye level, from the front, of a lone traveller in a long heavy coat with a steel shoulder plate, holding a drawn straight sword lowered at his right side, standing at the mouth of a narrow alley between ruined brick buildings. Broken rubble and fallen beams lie across the ground, and a torn cloth banner hangs in the foreground at the left edge of the frame. Scorch marks streak the walls, a shattered window frame hangs open on the second floor, and a broken cart lies on its side halfway down the alley. The ground is uneven, and his boots find footing between broken bricks. First he stands still and catches his breath, then he walks three slow steps forward over the rubble, as loose grit crunches and slides under his boots; finally he stops, lifts his head, and looks down the alley while the coat hem settles against his legs. His face is lean and tired, his jaw set, and his free left hand hangs loose at his side, fingers slightly curled. Dim dusk sky light from the gap in the broken skyline rakes across the left side of his shoulder plate and leaves the alley walls in deep shadow that keeps the brick texture. Colour palette: the coat folds and the gaps between the rubble are #0B1118, the shadowed building walls are #1E2A38, his shoulder plate is #3B5068, the haze in the far distance is #6B8299, and only the blade edge and the catchlights in his eyes are #E6F2FF. Thin haze drifts slowly through the far end of the alley, and a few flakes of ash float down through the air without settling. Small puddles between the stones hold a dull, still reflection of the sky. The camera pulls out with small amplitude at slow speed as he walks forward, keeping his full body in frame, and holds the final composition.

overall_soundscape: Low wind moving through the ruined alley, the banner cloth flapping softly, grit crunching and sliding under boots on each step, and a faint metallic tick as the sword shifts in his grip.

non_diegetic_music: N/A

pair_check.method: python: len(field.split()) == wc -w; shared sentences are the same Python string objects inserted into both arms, asserted present verbatim in both

self_check_notes: Shared light sentence is deliberately colour-free so the HEX arm gets no colour words from shared text.
'dusk' and 'low-saturation' are shared style cues present in both arms.
rater_brief: Dusk, ruined alley, a traveller with a lowered sword walks three steps and stops. Judge colour and artifacts only.

objective.mean_Lab: same run, meanLab (report a*, b* to see hue drift)
objective.noise_floor: palette dE76 has ~2 units of quantisation noise (lighting-and-color.md §E); differences < 2 count as ties
objective.scene_cuts: ffmpeg -i <code>.mp4 -vf "select='gt(scene,0.3)',showinfo" -f null - 2>&1 | grep -o 'pts_time:[0-9.]*'  (threshold 0.3 primary; also log 0.2 and 0.4)  (expect 0; single-shot prompt)

rubric.scale_note: 0 = absent/failed, 1 = partial/ambiguous, 2 = clearly present. Score each clip independently; never compare two clips side by side before all scores are written.

artifact.0: severe: limb/face melt, body splits, object morphs

palette_feel.0: warm or saturated, not cold blue

text_or_swatch_artifact.0: visible hex-like text, colour bars or swatches

decision.keep_rule_no_HEX: B card dE76 <= A + 2 in >= 2/3 seeds, or any A clip shows text/swatch artifact -> lighting-and-color.md keeps 'colour name + object, no HEX', marked '本機先導實測'.
decision.HEX_has_value: A card dE76 lower than B by > 2 in 3/3 seeds with no text artifact -> add HEX as an optional tested technique (not main rule) and rerun at 0.98MP once.
decision.structural_fail: a clip with a verified cut (detected at 0.3 AND 0.4) is scored structural-fail; that seed pair is excluded from the objective comparison and reported separately. If >= 2 seed pairs are excluded, the test is inconclusive.

independent_verification.computed_by: freeze_plans.py from the exact strings written
independent_verification.bash_cross_check: 2026-10-20 Git Bash wc -w on the extracted counted field, diff of overall_soundscape..non_diegetic_music block, grep -oiE music words: all matched these numbers
